Hi Jill — thanks, and congrats on getting close to procurement. Quick answers up front, then next steps below.

Short answers:
- Yes — Redwood supports tenant-scoped TTLs. Customers can set a per-tenant log TTL (30/90/365 days) through the console or API; default is 90 days for hosted accounts.
- We can produce a per-tenant deletion report that includes: time-window covered, object ids removed, and a signed attestation from our security team. The process is manual for ad-hoc requests and typically takes 3 business days; for high-volume/contracted requests we can automate.

What I attached: 
- HealthSync_SIG_partial_answers.pdf — an export with our SIG section answers and references to the log-retention controls.
- redacted-log-sample.json — a sample tenant export with PII fields removed.
- conditional-exception-template.docx — template we use to document approved retention exceptions.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the TTL you want to be the customer default (30 or 90).
2) If you need a one-off legal hold for a subset of tenants, we will:
   - Open a one-off exception ticket (HubSpot HS-4521).
   - Apply a scoped hold (no deletion for IDs listed) and provide a deletion attestation when released.
   - Provide the redacted export + signed attestation within 72 hours after hold release.

I copied Neha (security) and Marissa (CS) to align on evidence and timelines. If that plan works I can prepare a short addendum (DocuSign link) to include with your procurement pack.

Looks good to me. A few legal constraints to bake into the template: 

- Any customer-requested hold must include a business/ legal owner and an expiration date. Never accept an indefinite hold.
- We will accept limited-scope holds only where the customer provides the tenant IDs or clear selection criteria (e.g., all tenants in org X).
- Attestation language should say: "Redwood Inference removed/retained only the records specified in the exception and provides this attestation as of [date/time]."

Approve moving forward with Priyom's plan and Neha's tweaks. If the customer requests automated SLAs, route to SalesOps for pricing.
